# Canon: the canon checker

How the canon checker behaves now, and why. It is the canon of the package `@bigmistqke/canon`. Its terms and its claims are written in Alloy, and the statement of a claim, or of a term that defines a word, is said from its predicate by `canon generate`, so that the units can be checked against each other. [The canon skill](../../skills/canon/SKILL.md) describes the method.

<!-- toc:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
- [`@term checker`](#term-checker) — Checker is the program the canon describes.
- [`@term unit`](#term-unit) — A unit is an axiom, a fact, a spec, an exception, a bug, a conflict or a term.
- [`@term axiom`](#term-axiom) — An axiom is a unit that states a value: how the project wants the world of the people using it to be.
- [`@term fact`](#term-fact) — A fact is a unit that states how the platform under the project is, whatever the project does.
- [`@term spec`](#term-spec) — A spec is a unit that states what the system does, so that a test could contradict it.
- [`@term exception`](#term-exception) — An exception is a unit that states where a fact keeps a spec from holding fully.
- [`@term bug`](#term-bug) — A bug is a unit that states where the code breaks the spec it sits in.
- [`@term conflict`](#term-conflict) — A conflict is a unit that states where units of the canon cannot all hold, until the owner of the design rules which one does.
- [`@term term`](#term-term) — A term is a unit that states a word of the project's language: what the thing it names is.
- [`@term sit`](#term-sit) — A unit sits in the unit whose heading holds its own heading.
- [`@term derive`](#term-derive) — A unit derives from each unit a link on its "Derives from:" line names.
- [`@term link`](#term-link) — A unit links to each unit a link in its body names.
- [`@term cite`](#term-cite) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit) and every unit_2: unit_1 cites unit_2 exactly when unit_1 [sits in](#term-sit) unit_2 or [derives from](#term-derive) unit_2.
- [`@term finding`](#term-finding) — A finding is a freelancing, a misnesting, an untracking, a mistracking, an outdated tracking, an unpairing, an unpinning, an unexplained failure, an untesting, a rotting, an uncitation, a misaiming, an overreach, an orphaning, a misanchoring, a misindexing, a mislocation or a cycle.
- [`@term freelancing`](#term-freelancing) — A freelancing is a finding for a unit that makes a claim and cites nothing it derives from.
- [`@term misnesting`](#term-misnesting) — A misnesting is a finding for a unit that cites a kind of unit it may not cite.
- [`@term unfounded`](#term-unfounded) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): unit_1 is unfounded exactly when unit_1 is one of these: - a [spec](#term-spec) that [cites](#term-cite) no [axiom](#term-axiom) and cites no spec - an [exception](#term-exception) that cites no spec or cites no [fact](#term-fact) - a [bug](#term-bug) that cites no spec
- [`@term miscited`](#term-miscited) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): unit_1 is miscited exactly when unit_1 is one of these: - an [axiom](#term-axiom) that [cites](#term-cite) a unit that is not an axiom - a [fact](#term-fact) that cites a unit - a [spec](#term-spec) that cites a unit that is not an axiom, a spec or a fact - an [exception](#term-exception) that cites a unit that is not a spec or a fact - a [bug](#term-bug) that cites a unit that is not a spec - a [conflict](#term-conflict) that cites a unit - a [term](#term-term) that cites a unit
- [`@term depend`](#term-depend) — A unit depends on a unit when the unit cites the unit. A unit depends on a unit when the unit cites a unit that depends on the unit.
- [`@term circular`](#term-circular) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): unit_1 is circular exactly when unit_1 [cites](#term-cite) a unit that [depends on](#term-depend) unit_1.
- [`@term cycle`](#term-cycle) — A cycle is a finding for a unit that depends on itself.
- [`@term untracking`](#term-untracking) — An untracking is a finding for a bug or a conflict that names no issue.
- [`@term mistracking`](#term-mistracking) — A mistracking is a finding for a bug or a conflict that names an issue the tracker does not know, or one that is a pull request.
- [`@term outdated-tracking`](#term-outdated-tracking) — An outdated tracking is a finding for a bug or a conflict that names an issue the tracker has closed.
- [`@term unpairing`](#term-unpairing) — An unpairing is a finding for a conflict that sets fewer than two units against each other.
- [`@term unpinning`](#term-unpinning) — An unpinning is a finding for a plain test that checks a bug.
- [`@term unexplained-failure`](#term-unexplained-failure) — An unexplained failure is a finding for an expected failure that checks no bug and no exception.
- [`@term untesting`](#term-untesting) — An untesting is a finding for a leaf spec, an exception or a bug that no test checks.
- [`@term rotting`](#term-rotting) — A rotting is a finding for a tag that names no unit, names a file as well as a unit, or names an id that two documents declare, and for a pointer that names no target.
- [`@term uncitation`](#term-uncitation) — An uncitation is a finding for a test in a declared suite that carries no tag.
- [`@term misaiming`](#term-misaiming) — A misaiming is a finding for a test in a declared suite that checks a unit that is no claim.
- [`@term overreach`](#term-overreach) — An overreach is a finding for a test that checks a claim another claim refines.
- [`@term orphaning`](#term-orphaning) — An orphaning is a finding for a unit that nothing uses.
- [`@term misanchoring`](#term-misanchoring) — A misanchoring is a finding for a unit whose heading holds a word after its id, so the anchor the page renders is not the id a pointer names.
- [`@term misindexing`](#term-misindexing) — A misindexing is a finding for a document with no index, or with an index that does not match it.
- [`@term mislocation`](#term-mislocation) — A mislocation is a finding for a claim that names a site no source holds.
- [`@term claim`](#term-claim) — A claim is a spec, an exception or a bug.
- [`@term refined`](#term-refined) — For every [claim_1](#term-claim): claim_1 is refined exactly when a [spec](#term-spec) [sits in](#term-sit) claim_1 or an [exception](#term-exception) sits in claim_1.
- [`@term unguarded`](#term-unguarded) — For every [claim_1](#term-claim): claim_1 is unguarded exactly when claim_1 is not [refined](#term-refined) and is not [tested](#term-tested).
- [`@term adrift`](#term-adrift) — For every [test_1](#term-test): test_1 is adrift exactly when at least one of these holds: - [project](#term-project) [declares](#term-declare) test_1 and test_1 [carries](#term-carry) no [tag](#term-tag) - project declares test_1 and test_1 [checks](#term-check) a [unit](#term-unit) that is not a [claim](#term-claim) - test_1 checks a claim that is [refined](#term-refined)
- [`@term test`](#term-test) — A test is a plain test or an expected failure.
- [`@term project`](#term-project) — Project is the package whose canon field names the canon.
- [`@term declare`](#term-declare) — Project declares each test in each suite that the canon field of the project names.
- [`@term pointer`](#term-pointer) — A pointer is a file pointer or a fragment pointer.
- [`@term file-pointer`](#term-file-pointer) — A file pointer is a pointer with no fragment: it names a [file](#term-file).
- [`@term fragment-pointer`](#term-fragment-pointer) — A fragment pointer is a pointer with a fragment, after a `#`: it names the unit or the [section](#term-section) whose id the fragment holds, in the file its path names.
- [`@term target`](#term-target) — A target is a unit, a section or a file.
- [`@term section`](#term-section) — A section is an element with an id that names no unit.
- [`@term file`](#term-file) — A file is a file of the project.
- [`@term used`](#term-used) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): unit_1 is used exactly when another unit [sits in](#term-sit) unit_1, a [pointer](#term-pointer) [names](#term-name) unit_1 or a [tag](#term-tag) names unit_1.
- [`@term trailer`](#term-trailer) — A trailer is a word that follows the id in the heading of a unit.
- [`@term repeat`](#term-repeat) — A unit repeats what spells the id of the unit in a heading of another unit.
- [`@term follow`](#term-follow) — A trailer follows the unit whose heading holds the trailer.
- [`@term document`](#term-document) — A document is a file that the canon field of the project names.
- [`@term index`](#term-index) — An index is the generated table of contents of a document.
- [`@term hold`](#term-hold) — A document holds each unit and each index in the document. A source holds each symbol that its code declares.
- [`@term match`](#term-match) — An index matches the document that generate writes the index for.
- [`@term site`](#term-site) — A site is a symbol in a source, as the site line of a claim writes it.
- [`@term source`](#term-source) — A source is a module in the sources that the canon field of the project names.
- [`@term code-span`](#term-code-span) — A code span is text between backticks in a document.
- [`@term comment`](#term-comment) — A comment is a comment in a source.
- [`@term tag`](#term-tag) — A tag is a line of the documentation comment of a test.
- [`@term carry`](#term-carry) — A test carries each tag in the documentation comment of the test.
- [`@term plain-test`](#term-plain-test) — A plain test is a test that passes when what it checks holds.
- [`@term expected-failure`](#term-expected-failure) — An expected failure is a test that is marked to fail, with `it.fails` or `test.fails`: it fails until the defect it checks is fixed.
- [`@term check`](#term-check) — For every [test_1](#term-test) and every [unit_1](#term-unit): test_1 checks unit_1 exactly when test_1 [carries](#term-carry) a [tag](#term-tag) that [names](#term-name) unit_1.
- [`@term issue`](#term-issue) — An issue is an entry of the tracker of the project.
- [`@term tracker`](#term-tracker) — Tracker is the issue tracker the scope of the project names.
- [`@term name`](#term-name) — A bug names each issue that the issue line of the bug names.
- [`@term tested`](#term-tested) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): unit_1 is tested exactly when at least one of these holds: - a [test](#term-test) [checks](#term-check) unit_1 - unit_1 is a [spec](#term-spec) and a test checks a [bug](#term-bug) that [sits in](#term-sit) unit_1
- [`@term paired`](#term-paired) — For every [conflict_1](#term-conflict): conflict_1 is paired exactly when conflict_1 [names](#term-name) a [unit](#term-unit) and names another unit.
- [`@term hidden`](#term-hidden) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): unit_1 is hidden exactly when unit_1 is one of these: - a [bug](#term-bug) that [names](#term-name) no [issue](#term-issue), names an issue that [tracker](#term-tracker) does not know, names an issue that tracker has closed or is not [tested](#term-tested) - a [conflict](#term-conflict) that names no issue, names an issue that tracker does not know, names an issue that tracker has closed or is not [paired](#term-paired)
- [`@term misleading`](#term-misleading) — For every [test_1](#term-test): test_1 is misleading exactly when test_1 is one of these: - an [expected failure](#term-expected-failure) that [checks](#term-check) no [bug](#term-bug) and checks no [exception](#term-exception) - a [plain test](#term-plain-test) that checks a bug
- [`@term plugin`](#term-plugin) — A plugin is a package that adds commands to the checker, and that a document asks for by the name of the package.
- [`@term command`](#term-command) — A command is a word after `canon` on the command line, and asks the checker for one job.
- [`@term frontmatter`](#term-frontmatter) — A frontmatter is the block between two lines of three dashes at the top of a document, which names the plugins the document asks for.
- [`@term entry`](#term-entry) — An entry is one string of the list of plugins in a frontmatter.
- [`@term list`](#term-list) — For every [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and every [plugin_1](#term-plugin): frontmatter_1 lists plugin_1 exactly when frontmatter_1 holds an [entry](#term-entry) that spells plugin_1.
- [`@term flaw`](#term-flaw) — A flaw is a mistake that makes a frontmatter unreadable.
- [`@term apply`](#term-apply) — For every [plugin_1](#term-plugin) and every [document_1](#term-document): plugin_1 applies to document_1 exactly when at least one of these holds: - plugin_1 is a plugin inside the package of the [checker](#term-checker) and document_1 starts with no [listing frontmatter](#term-frontmatter) - document_1 starts with a listing frontmatter that [lists](#term-list) plugin_1
- [`@term run`](#term-run) — A run is one call of the checker on the command line, with a command and the documents it names.
- [`@term call`](#term-call) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [plugin_1](#term-plugin): run_1 calls plugin_1 exactly when all of these hold: - run_1 asks for a [command](#term-command) that plugin_1 adds - plugin_1 is a plugin inside the package of the [checker](#term-checker) or [applies](#term-apply) to a [document](#term-document)
- [`@term availability`](#term-availability) — For every [command_1](#term-command): command_1 is available exactly when at least one of these holds: - command_1 is a command that the [checker](#term-checker) has of its own - an [inside plugin](#term-plugin) adds command_1 - there are installed_plugin_1 and [document_1](#term-document) such that installed_plugin_1 [applies](#term-apply) to document_1 and adds command_1
- [`@term statement`](#term-statement) — A statement is the quote under the heading of a unit that says in words what the unit claims.
- [`@term word`](#term-word) — A word is a signature, a field of a signature or a predicate that a document declares in its model, and that its readings say.
- [`@term formula`](#term-formula) — A formula is a piece of Alloy that states a claim, and that the checker says in words.
- [`@term quantified-formula`](#term-quantified-formula) — A quantified formula is a formula that declares variables, and the checker names them and says their types.
- [`@term quantifier`](#term-quantifier) — A quantifier is a formula that declares a variable and says something of it, which the checker may say as a noun phrase.
- [`@term fit`](#term-fit) — For every [quantifier_1](#term-quantifier): quantifier_1 fits a noun phrase exactly when all of these hold: - quantifier_1 is not a quantifier whose reading says the variable twice - quantifier_1 is not a quantifier with no fact for its variable beside another thing - quantifier_1 is not a quantifier that says no variable differs from another and holds a condition - quantifier_1 is not a quantifier whose condition is not about its variable
- [`@term predicate-call`](#term-predicate-call) — A predicate call is a formula that names a predicate and gives its arguments.
- [`@term parsed-formula`](#term-parsed-formula) — A parsed formula is a formula as the parser reads it: its operators, their operands and their grouping.
- [`@term definition-passage`](#term-definition-passage) — A definition is a predicate with a body that the checker says as what its name means exactly when the body holds.
- [`@term by-kind`](#term-by-kind) — For every [definition_1](#term-definition-passage): definition_1 can be said kind by kind exactly when all of these hold: - definition_1 is not a definition with an alternative that does not begin with its kind - definition_1 is not a definition with a run of and beside another alternative of its kind - definition_1 is not a definition with an alternative that says something about another unit
- [`@term linked-formula`](#term-linked-formula) — A linked formula is a formula that has a word whose reading a unit holds, and the statement may link that word.
- [`@term series`](#term-series) — A series is a run of clauses, or a rule of two sides, that the checker says as a sentence, as bullets or on one line.
- [`@term sentenceable`](#term-sentenceable) — For every [list_1](#term-series): list_1 can be put in a sentence exactly when all of these hold: - list_1 has three clauses or fewer - list_1 has only items that are one clause - list_1 has no item that holds a comma or has two clauses or fewer - list_1 fits a line when it is put in a sentence
- [`@term line`](#term-line) — A line is one line of a table of readings, which gives a word of the logic its sentences.
- [`@term scenario`](#term-scenario) — A scenario is a situation that a unit says must be possible while every unit of the canon holds.
- [`@term search`](#term-search) — A search is one run of the analyzer over some units: it asks whether they can hold, with a scenario or without.
- [`@term group`](#term-group) — A group is a set of units linked through the words they share.
- [`@term heading`](#term-heading) — A heading is a line of a document that starts with hashes and opens a part of it.
- [`@term extent`](#term-extent) — The extent of a unit is the part of the document from its heading up to the next heading of its level or above.
- [`@term own-text`](#term-own-text) — The own text of a unit is the text between its heading and its first nested heading.
- [`@term fence`](#term-fence) — A fence is a block of lines between two lines of backticks or tildes, which holds logic or a table of readings.
- [`@axiom every-claim-says-what-it-follows-from`](#axiom-every-claim-says-what-it-follows-from) — All of these hold: - for every [unit_1](#term-unit): when unit_1 is [unfounded](#term-unfounded), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for unit_1 - for every unit_1: when unit_1 is [miscited](#term-miscited), checker reports a finding for unit_1 - for every unit_1: when unit_1 is [circular](#term-circular), checker reports a finding for unit_1.
  - [`@spec an-unfounded-unit-is-freelancing`](#spec-an-unfounded-unit-is-freelancing) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when unit_1 is [unfounded](#term-unfounded), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [freelancing](#term-freelancing) for unit_1.
    - [`@spec a-spec-cites-an-axiom-or-a-spec`](#spec-a-spec-cites-an-axiom-or-a-spec) — For every [spec_1](#term-spec): when spec_1 [cites](#term-cite) no [axiom](#term-axiom) and cites no spec, [checker](#term-checker) reports a [freelancing](#term-freelancing) for spec_1.
    - [`@spec an-exception-cites-a-spec`](#spec-an-exception-cites-a-spec) — For every [exception_1](#term-exception): when exception_1 [cites](#term-cite) no [spec](#term-spec), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [freelancing](#term-freelancing) for exception_1.
    - [`@spec an-exception-cites-a-fact`](#spec-an-exception-cites-a-fact) — For every [exception_1](#term-exception): when exception_1 [cites](#term-cite) no [fact](#term-fact), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [freelancing](#term-freelancing) for exception_1.
    - [`@spec a-bug-cites-a-spec`](#spec-a-bug-cites-a-spec) — For every [bug_1](#term-bug): when bug_1 [cites](#term-cite) no [spec](#term-spec), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [freelancing](#term-freelancing) for bug_1.
    - [`@bug a-link-in-the-body-counts-as-a-citation`](#bug-a-link-in-the-body-counts-as-a-citation) — When a spec links to an axiom, and the spec cites no axiom, and the spec cites no spec, checker reports no freelancing for the spec.
  - [`@spec a-miscited-unit-is-misnested`](#spec-a-miscited-unit-is-misnested) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when unit_1 is [miscited](#term-miscited), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misnesting](#term-misnesting) for unit_1.
    - [`@spec an-axiom-cites-only-axioms`](#spec-an-axiom-cites-only-axioms) — For every [axiom_1](#term-axiom): when axiom_1 [cites](#term-cite) a [unit](#term-unit) that is not an axiom, [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misnesting](#term-misnesting) for axiom_1.
    - [`@spec a-fact-cites-nothing`](#spec-a-fact-cites-nothing) — For every [fact_1](#term-fact): when fact_1 [cites](#term-cite) a [unit](#term-unit), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misnesting](#term-misnesting) for fact_1.
    - [`@spec a-spec-cites-only-axioms-specs-and-facts`](#spec-a-spec-cites-only-axioms-specs-and-facts) — For every [spec_1](#term-spec): when spec_1 [cites](#term-cite) a [unit](#term-unit) that is not an [axiom](#term-axiom), a spec or a [fact](#term-fact), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misnesting](#term-misnesting) for spec_1.
    - [`@spec an-exception-cites-only-specs-and-facts`](#spec-an-exception-cites-only-specs-and-facts) — For every [exception_1](#term-exception): when exception_1 [cites](#term-cite) a [unit](#term-unit) that is not a [spec](#term-spec) or a [fact](#term-fact), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misnesting](#term-misnesting) for exception_1.
    - [`@spec a-bug-cites-only-specs`](#spec-a-bug-cites-only-specs) — For every [bug_1](#term-bug): when bug_1 [cites](#term-cite) a [unit](#term-unit) that is not a [spec](#term-spec), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misnesting](#term-misnesting) for bug_1.
    - [`@spec a-conflict-cites-nothing`](#spec-a-conflict-cites-nothing) — For every [conflict_1](#term-conflict): when conflict_1 [cites](#term-cite) a [unit](#term-unit), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misnesting](#term-misnesting) for conflict_1.
    - [`@spec a-term-cites-nothing`](#spec-a-term-cites-nothing) — For every [term_1](#term-term): when term_1 [cites](#term-cite) a [unit](#term-unit), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misnesting](#term-misnesting) for term_1.
    - [`@bug a-derives-from-line-is-not-checked-for-its-kind`](#bug-a-derives-from-line-is-not-checked-for-its-kind) — When a fact derives from a unit, and the fact sits in no unit, checker reports no misnesting for the fact.
  - [`@spec a-unit-does-not-depend-on-itself`](#spec-a-unit-does-not-depend-on-itself) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when unit_1 is [circular](#term-circular), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [cycle](#term-cycle) for unit_1.
- [`@axiom a-known-defect-stays-in-sight`](#axiom-a-known-defect-stays-in-sight) — All of these hold: - for every [bug_1](#term-bug): when bug_1 is [hidden](#term-hidden), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for bug_1 - for every [conflict_1](#term-conflict): when conflict_1 is hidden, checker reports a finding for conflict_1 - for every [test_1](#term-test): when test_1 is [misleading](#term-misleading), checker reports a finding for test_1.
  - [`@spec a-hidden-bug-is-reported`](#spec-a-hidden-bug-is-reported) — For every [bug_1](#term-bug): when bug_1 is [hidden](#term-hidden), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for bug_1.
    - [`@spec a-bug-names-an-issue`](#spec-a-bug-names-an-issue) — For every [bug_1](#term-bug): when bug_1 [names](#term-name) no [issue](#term-issue), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [untracking](#term-untracking) for bug_1.
    - [`@spec a-bug-names-an-issue-the-tracker-knows`](#spec-a-bug-names-an-issue-the-tracker-knows) — For every [bug_1](#term-bug): when bug_1 [names](#term-name) an [issue](#term-issue) that [tracker](#term-tracker) does not know, [checker](#term-checker) reports a [mistracking](#term-mistracking) for bug_1.
    - [`@spec a-bug-names-an-open-issue`](#spec-a-bug-names-an-open-issue) — For every [bug_1](#term-bug): when bug_1 [names](#term-name) an [issue](#term-issue) that [tracker](#term-tracker) has closed, [checker](#term-checker) reports an [outdated tracking](#term-outdated-tracking) for bug_1.
    - [`@spec a-bug-is-tested`](#spec-a-bug-is-tested) — For every [bug_1](#term-bug): when bug_1 is not [tested](#term-tested), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [untesting](#term-untesting) for bug_1.
  - [`@spec a-hidden-conflict-is-reported`](#spec-a-hidden-conflict-is-reported) — For every [conflict_1](#term-conflict): when conflict_1 is [hidden](#term-hidden), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for conflict_1.
    - [`@spec a-conflict-names-an-issue`](#spec-a-conflict-names-an-issue) — For every [conflict_1](#term-conflict): when conflict_1 [names](#term-name) no [issue](#term-issue), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [untracking](#term-untracking) for conflict_1.
    - [`@spec a-conflict-names-an-issue-the-tracker-knows`](#spec-a-conflict-names-an-issue-the-tracker-knows) — For every [conflict_1](#term-conflict): when conflict_1 [names](#term-name) an [issue](#term-issue) that [tracker](#term-tracker) does not know, [checker](#term-checker) reports a [mistracking](#term-mistracking) for conflict_1.
    - [`@spec a-conflict-names-an-open-issue`](#spec-a-conflict-names-an-open-issue) — For every [conflict_1](#term-conflict): when conflict_1 [names](#term-name) an [issue](#term-issue) that [tracker](#term-tracker) has closed, [checker](#term-checker) reports an [outdated tracking](#term-outdated-tracking) for conflict_1.
    - [`@spec a-conflict-names-two-units`](#spec-a-conflict-names-two-units) — For every [conflict_1](#term-conflict): when conflict_1 is not [paired](#term-paired), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [unpairing](#term-unpairing) for conflict_1.
  - [`@spec a-misleading-test-is-reported`](#spec-a-misleading-test-is-reported) — For every [test_1](#term-test): when test_1 is [misleading](#term-misleading), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for test_1.
    - [`@spec an-expected-failure-checks-a-bug-or-an-exception`](#spec-an-expected-failure-checks-a-bug-or-an-exception) — For every [expected_failure_1](#term-expected-failure): when expected_failure_1 [checks](#term-check) no [bug](#term-bug) and checks no [exception](#term-exception), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [unexplained failure](#term-unexplained-failure) for expected_failure_1.

- [`@axiom a-canon-cannot-go-out-of-date-unnoticed`](#axiom-a-canon-cannot-go-out-of-date-unnoticed) — All of these hold: - for every [claim_1](#term-claim): when claim_1 is [unguarded](#term-unguarded), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for claim_1 - for every [tag_1](#term-tag): when tag_1 [names](#term-name) no [unit](#term-unit), checker reports a finding for tag_1 - for every [test_1](#term-test): when test_1 is [adrift](#term-adrift), checker reports a finding for test_1 - for every [pointer_1](#term-pointer): when pointer_1 names no [target](#term-target), checker reports a finding for pointer_1 - for every unit_1: when unit_1 is not [used](#term-used) and is not a [conflict](#term-conflict), checker reports a finding for unit_1 - for every unit_1: when a [trailer](#term-trailer) [follows](#term-follow) unit_1, checker reports a finding for unit_1 - for every [document_1](#term-document): when document_1 [holds](#term-hold) a unit and holds no [index](#term-index), checker reports a finding for document_1 - for every document_1: when document_1 holds an index that does not [match](#term-match) document_1, checker reports a finding for document_1 - for every claim_1: when claim_1 names a [site](#term-site) that no [source](#term-source) holds, checker reports a finding for claim_1 - for every unit_1: when unit_1 [repeats](#term-repeat) a unit, checker reports a finding for unit_1.
  - [`@spec an-unguarded-claim-is-untested`](#spec-an-unguarded-claim-is-untested) — For every [claim_1](#term-claim): when claim_1 is [unguarded](#term-unguarded), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [untesting](#term-untesting) for claim_1.
  - [`@spec a-tag-names-a-unit`](#spec-a-tag-names-a-unit) — For every [tag_1](#term-tag): when tag_1 [names](#term-name) no [unit](#term-unit), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [rotting](#term-rotting) for tag_1.
  - [`@spec an-adrift-test-is-reported`](#spec-an-adrift-test-is-reported) — For every [test_1](#term-test): when test_1 is [adrift](#term-adrift), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for test_1.

    - [`@spec a-declared-test-checks-only-claims`](#spec-a-declared-test-checks-only-claims) — For every [test_1](#term-test): when [project](#term-project) [declares](#term-declare) test_1 and test_1 [checks](#term-check) a [unit](#term-unit) that is not a [claim](#term-claim), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misaiming](#term-misaiming) for test_1.
    - [`@spec a-test-checks-only-leaves`](#spec-a-test-checks-only-leaves) — For every [test_1](#term-test): when test_1 [checks](#term-check) a [claim](#term-claim) that is [refined](#term-refined), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [overreach](#term-overreach) for test_1.
  - [`@spec a-pointer-names-a-target`](#spec-a-pointer-names-a-target) — For every [pointer_1](#term-pointer): when pointer_1 [names](#term-name) no [target](#term-target), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [rotting](#term-rotting) for pointer_1.
    - [`@bug a-file-pointer-is-not-checked`](#bug-a-file-pointer-is-not-checked) — When a file pointer names no target, checker reports no rotting for the file pointer.

  - [`@spec a-site-is-held-by-a-source`](#spec-a-site-is-held-by-a-source) — For every [claim_1](#term-claim): when claim_1 [names](#term-name) a [site](#term-site) that no [source](#term-source) [holds](#term-hold), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [mislocation](#term-mislocation) for claim_1.

- [`@axiom a-check-the-project-asked-for-is-never-dropped-silently`](#axiom-a-check-the-project-asked-for-is-never-dropped-silently) — For every [run_1](#term-run): when at least one of these holds: - there are [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and [missing_plugin_1](#term-plugin) such that frontmatter_1 [lists](#term-list) missing_plugin_1 - there is a [document_1](#term-document) such that [checker](#term-checker) reports that document_1 has a frontmatter it cannot read - run_1 asks for a [command](#term-command) that is not [available](#term-availability) - run_1 gets code 2 from a plugin then run_1 exits with code 2.
  - [`@spec a-document-gets-the-plugins-it-asks-for`](#spec-a-document-gets-the-plugins-it-asks-for) — For every [plugin_1](#term-plugin) and every [document_1](#term-document): all of these hold: - when plugin_1 [applies](#term-apply) to document_1, [checker](#term-checker) runs plugin_1 over document_1 - when the command line of a [run](#term-run) does not name document_1 and checker runs plugin_1 over document_1, plugin_1 applies to document_1
    - [`@spec a-document-with-no-plugins-list-gets-the-plugins-inside-the-package`](#spec-a-document-with-no-plugins-list-gets-the-plugins-inside-the-package) — For every [inside_plugin_1](#term-plugin) and every [document_1](#term-document): when document_1 starts with no [listing frontmatter](#term-frontmatter), [checker](#term-checker) runs inside_plugin_1 over document_1.

    - [`@spec an-empty-list-asks-for-no-plugin`](#spec-an-empty-list-asks-for-no-plugin) — For every [plugin_1](#term-plugin) and every [document_1](#term-document) and every [listing_frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter): when all of these hold: - document_1 starts with listing_frontmatter_1 - listing_frontmatter_1 holds no [entry](#term-entry) - the command line of a [run](#term-run) does not name document_1 then [checker](#term-checker) does not run plugin_1 over document_1.
    - [`@spec a-document-named-on-the-command-line-is-checked-whatever-its-frontmatter-says`](#spec-a-document-named-on-the-command-line-is-checked-whatever-its-frontmatter-says) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [plugin_1](#term-plugin) and every given_document_1: when run_1 [calls](#term-call) plugin_1, [checker](#term-checker) runs plugin_1 over given_document_1.
  - [`@spec a-frontmatter-lists-what-is-written-in-it`](#spec-a-frontmatter-lists-what-is-written-in-it) — For every [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and every [entry_1](#term-entry): when frontmatter_1 holds entry_1, then all of these hold: - frontmatter_1 is a frontmatter with a plugins key - frontmatter_1 has entry_1 between its brackets or has entry_1 after a dash
    - [`@spec an-inline-list-holds-the-entries-between-its-brackets`](#spec-an-inline-list-holds-the-entries-between-its-brackets) — For every [inline_frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and every [entry_1](#term-entry): when inline_frontmatter_1 has entry_1 between its brackets, inline_frontmatter_1 holds entry_1.
    - [`@spec a-dashed-list-holds-the-entries-after-its-dashes`](#spec-a-dashed-list-holds-the-entries-after-its-dashes) — For every [dashed_frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and every [entry_1](#term-entry): when dashed_frontmatter_1 has entry_1 after a dash, dashed_frontmatter_1 holds entry_1.

    - [`@spec a-frontmatter-with-no-plugins-key-holds-no-entry`](#spec-a-frontmatter-with-no-plugins-key-holds-no-entry) — For every [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter): when frontmatter_1 is not a frontmatter with a plugins key, frontmatter_1 holds no [entry](#term-entry).

  - [`@spec a-flawed-frontmatter-is-refused`](#spec-a-flawed-frontmatter-is-refused) — For every [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter): when at least one of these holds: - frontmatter_1 has the [flaw](#term-flaw) of an entry that starts with an at sign outside quotes - frontmatter_1 has the flaw of a key that the [checker](#term-checker) does not know - frontmatter_1 has the flaw of a list that is not closed - frontmatter_1 has the flaw of a string that is not closed - frontmatter_1 has the flaw of a key that appears twice then frontmatter_1 is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.
    - [`@spec a-misquoted-entry-is-refused`](#spec-a-misquoted-entry-is-refused) — For every [misquoted_frontmatter_1](#term-flaw): misquoted_frontmatter_1 is a [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter) that the [checker](#term-checker) cannot read.

    - [`@spec a-key-the-checker-does-not-know-is-refused`](#spec-a-key-the-checker-does-not-know-is-refused) — For every [foreign_frontmatter_1](#term-flaw): foreign_frontmatter_1 is a [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter) that the [checker](#term-checker) cannot read.
    - [`@spec a-list-that-is-not-closed-is-refused`](#spec-a-list-that-is-not-closed-is-refused) — For every [unclosed_frontmatter_1](#term-flaw): unclosed_frontmatter_1 is a [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter) that the [checker](#term-checker) cannot read.
    - [`@spec a-string-that-is-not-closed-is-refused`](#spec-a-string-that-is-not-closed-is-refused) — For every [unterminated_frontmatter_1](#term-flaw): unterminated_frontmatter_1 is a [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter) that the [checker](#term-checker) cannot read.
    - [`@spec a-key-written-twice-is-refused`](#spec-a-key-written-twice-is-refused) — For every [doubled_frontmatter_1](#term-flaw): doubled_frontmatter_1 is a [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter) that the [checker](#term-checker) cannot read.
  - [`@spec a-refused-frontmatter-fails-the-run`](#spec-a-refused-frontmatter-fails-the-run) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [document_1](#term-document) and every [refused_frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter): when document_1 starts with refused_frontmatter_1, [checker](#term-checker) reports that document_1 has a frontmatter it cannot read and run_1 exits with code 2.

    - [`@spec a-report-of-an-unreadable-frontmatter-stops-the-run`](#spec-a-report-of-an-unreadable-frontmatter-stops-the-run) — For every [run_1](#term-run): when there is a [document_1](#term-document) such that [checker](#term-checker) reports that document_1 has a [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter) it cannot read, run_1 exits with code 2.
  - [`@spec a-plugin-the-project-lacks-fails-the-run`](#spec-a-plugin-the-project-lacks-fails-the-run) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and every [missing_plugin_1](#term-plugin): when frontmatter_1 [lists](#term-list) missing_plugin_1, [checker](#term-checker) reports that the project lacks missing_plugin_1 and run_1 exits with code 2.
    - [`@spec a-missing-plugin-is-reported`](#spec-a-missing-plugin-is-reported) — For every [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and every [missing_plugin_1](#term-plugin): when frontmatter_1 [lists](#term-list) missing_plugin_1, [checker](#term-checker) reports that the project lacks missing_plugin_1.
    - [`@spec a-missing-plugin-stops-the-run`](#spec-a-missing-plugin-stops-the-run) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and every [missing_plugin_1](#term-plugin): when frontmatter_1 [lists](#term-list) missing_plugin_1, run_1 exits with code 2.
    - [`@spec the-report-of-a-missing-plugin-offers-the-plugins-inside`](#spec-the-report-of-a-missing-plugin-offers-the-plugins-inside) — For every [plugin_1](#term-plugin) and every inside_plugin_1: when [checker](#term-checker) reports that the project lacks plugin_1, checker offers inside_plugin_1 in place of plugin_1.
  - [`@spec an-unknown-command-fails-the-run`](#spec-an-unknown-command-fails-the-run) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [command_1](#term-command): when run_1 asks for command_1 and command_1 is not [available](#term-availability), [checker](#term-checker) reports command_1 as an unknown command and run_1 exits with code 2.
    - [`@spec a-command-that-is-not-available-is-reported-as-unknown`](#spec-a-command-that-is-not-available-is-reported-as-unknown) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [command_1](#term-command): when run_1 asks for command_1 and command_1 is not [available](#term-availability), [checker](#term-checker) reports command_1 as an unknown command.
    - [`@spec a-command-that-is-not-available-stops-the-run`](#spec-a-command-that-is-not-available-stops-the-run) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [command_1](#term-command): when run_1 asks for command_1 and command_1 is not [available](#term-availability), run_1 exits with code 2.
    - [`@spec an-available-command-is-not-reported-as-unknown`](#spec-an-available-command-is-not-reported-as-unknown) — For every [command_1](#term-command): when command_1 is [available](#term-availability), [checker](#term-checker) does not report command_1 as an unknown command.
  - [`@spec every-plugin-a-run-calls-runs`](#spec-every-plugin-a-run-calls-runs) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [plugin_1](#term-plugin): when run_1 [calls](#term-call) plugin_1, run_1 gets code 0 from plugin_1, gets code 1 from plugin_1 or gets code 2 from plugin_1.
  - [`@spec a-run-exits-with-the-worst-code-of-its-plugins`](#spec-a-run-exits-with-the-worst-code-of-its-plugins) — For every [run_1](#term-run): all of these hold: - when run_1 gets code 2 from a [plugin](#term-plugin), run_1 exits with code 2 - when run_1 gets code 1 from a plugin and gets code 2 from no plugin, run_1 exits with code 1
    - [`@spec a-plugin-that-could-not-run-stops-the-run`](#spec-a-plugin-that-could-not-run-stops-the-run) — For every [run_1](#term-run): when run_1 gets code 2 from a [plugin](#term-plugin), run_1 exits with code 2.
    - [`@spec a-finding-fails-the-run`](#spec-a-finding-fails-the-run) — For every [run_1](#term-run): when run_1 gets code 1 from a [plugin](#term-plugin) and gets code 2 from no plugin, run_1 exits with code 1.

  - [`@spec a-frontmatter-changes-nothing-but-the-plugins-of-its-document`](#spec-a-frontmatter-changes-nothing-but-the-plugins-of-its-document) — For every [document_1](#term-document) and every document_2: when document_1 is document_2 without its [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter), then all of these hold: - for every [unit_1](#term-unit): all of these hold: - when document_2 [holds](#term-hold) unit_1, document_1 holds unit_1 - when document_1 holds unit_1, document_2 holds unit_1 - when [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for document_2, checker reports a finding for document_1 - when checker reports a finding for document_1, checker reports a finding for document_2
